gallery.filename: USS Higbee (DD-806) under repair at Subic Bay in 1972.jpg
gallery.title: File:USS Higbee (DD-806) under repair at Subic Bay in 1972.jpg
gallery.credit: U.S. Navy All Hands magazine October 1972, p. 30.
gallery.source: USS Higbee (DD-806) under repair at Subic Bay in 1972
gallery.description: The U.S. Navy destroyer USS Higbee (DD-806) under repair in Floating Drydock AFDM-6 at the Ship Repair Facility at Subic Bay, Philippines, circa in May 1972. On 19 April 1972, Higbee became the first U.S. warship to be bombed during the Vietnam War, when two North Vietnamese Air Force Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-17s from the 923rd Fighter Regiment attacked, one of which, piloted by Le Xuan Di, dropped a 250 kilogram bomb onto Higbee's rear 127 mm gun mount, destroying it. The 127 mm gun crew had been outside their turret, due to a misfire within the mount, when the air attack occurred, which resulted in the wounding of four U.S. sailors.
categories: Ships at Naval Base Subic Bay

gallery.filename: Task Force 77 in South China Sea, 1965.jpg
gallery.title: File:Task Force 77 in South China Sea, 1965.jpg
gallery.description: The U.S. Navy Task Force 77 operating in the South China Sea, March 1965. It had recently launched strikes against North Vietnam. Carriers present are (clockwise from bottom): Ranger (CVA-61), Yorktown (CVS-10), Coral Sea (CVA-43) and Hancock (CVA-19). The guided missile cruiser Canberra (CAG-2) is in the center of the formation. The destroyer screen includes: England (DLG-22), Gurke (DD-783), Rogers (DD-876), Walker (DD-517), O'Bannon (DD-450), Somers (DD-947), Jenkins (DD-447), John A. Bole (DD-755), Higbee (DD-806), Buck (DD-761), Joseph Strauss (DDG-16) and Ernest G. Small (DD-838).This photograph was specially posed, and does not represent a normal operating formation.

gallery.filename: Steam locomotive whistle aboard USS Higbee (DD-806), circa in 1970.png
gallery.title: File:Steam locomotive whistle aboard USS Higbee (DD-806), circa in 1970.png
gallery.description: During the Vietnam war era, the U.S. Navy destroyer USS Higbee (DD-806) had a steam locomotive whistle attached to a port side steam fitting on the main deck amidships. The whistle was used to salute the providing ship following underway replenishment. The plume of steam marks the whistle location in this salute following refueling from the guided missile cruiser USS Chicago (CG-11), circa in 1970.

gallery.filename: USS Higbee (DD-806) leaving Subic Bay in 1972.jpg
gallery.title: File:USS Higbee (DD-806) leaving Subic Bay in 1972.jpg
gallery.description: The U.S. Navy destroyer USS Higbee (DD-806) leaving the Ship Repair Facility at Subic Bay, Philippines, in 1972. On 19 April 1972, Higbee became the first U.S. warship to be bombed during the Vietnam War, when two North Vietnamese Air Force Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-17s from the 923rd Fighter Regiment attacked, one of which, piloted by Le Xuan Di, dropped a 250 kilogram bomb onto Higbee's rear 127 mm gun mount, destroying it. gallery.artist: National Museum of the U.S. Navy
gallery.description: 330-PS-6386 ( NPC 19834):   Presentation of the battle flag USS Higbee (DDR 806).   Left to right:  Rear Admiral Lamont Pugh, MC, USN; Surgeon General and Chief of BUMED; Captain Winnie Gibson, NC, USN, Director of the Navy Nurse Corps; Captain Wade De Weese, USN, (Retired), Director, U.S. Naval Academy Museum; and Captain Lindsey Williamson, USN, former Commanding Officer of USS Higbee, now with Bureau of Personnel.   Note, USS Higbee was the first U.S. Navy warship to be named for a female member of the U.S. Navy.  Photograph released December 3, 1953.  (4/14/2015).
